STEP 01
1
본문과 해석
본문 + 해석 + 핵심 어휘 정리
원문 PASSAGE
1The major consumer of oil is transport. 2But consider what has happened over the last 30 years or so to the technology involved in producing the internal combustion engine. 3Because oil is expensive, car engines today are far more efficient in their consumption of fuel (and far less polluting) than they were in 1972. 4The cars that Asia buys tomorrow will certainly not be anything like those Americans use today. 5Americans will not buy today's cars tomorrow either. 6In fact, if the price of oil does rise much further then fuel cell technology (which produces energy from water!) will receive yet another momentum. 7The big car multinationals have already produced the prototype motors — they are currently racing to try and get prices down and engine performances up. 8Their future profits depend upon it. 9Imagine now if there is a breakthrough in fuel cell technology. 10What would happen to oil prices? 11They would fall dramatically — signalling much less demand than supply — and oil companies and OPEC oil producers would stand to lose much income. 12The fact that this threat is real is driving the producers to look for alternative sources of income. 13The 'oil majors' have diversified and are now more energy companies than oil companies these days and the OPEC countries are urgently attempting to exclude other industries.
전체 해석
1석유의 주요 소비처는 운송이다. 2그러나 지난 30여 년 동안 내연기관을 생산하는 데 관련된 기술에 무슨 일이 일어났는지 생각해 보라. 3석유가 비싸기 때문에, 오늘날 자동차 엔진은 1972년보다 연료 소비에서 훨씬 더 효율적이다(그리고 훨씬 덜 오염시킨다). 4아시아가 내일 살 자동차는 분명히 오늘날 미국인이 쓰는 자동차와 전혀 같지 않을 것이다. 5미국인들도 오늘날의 자동차를 내일 사지는 않을 것이다. 6사실, 만약 유가가 훨씬 더 오른다면 (물에서 에너지를 만들어 내는!) 연료전지 기술은 또 한 번의 추진력을 받을 것이다. 7거대 자동차 다국적 기업들은 이미 시제품 모터를 만들었고, 가격을 낮추고 엔진 성능을 높이기 위해 현재 경쟁하고 있다. 8그들의 미래 이익이 그것에 달려 있다. 9이제 연료전지 기술에 획기적 돌파구가 생긴다고 상상해 보라. 10유가에는 무슨 일이 일어날까? 11유가는 급격히 떨어질 것이고 — 공급보다 수요가 훨씬 적음을 알리며 — 석유 회사들과 OPEC 석유 생산자들은 많은 수입을 잃게 될 것이다. 12이 위협이 실재한다는 사실이 생산자들로 하여금 대체 수입원을 찾도록 몰아가고 있다. 13'석유 메이저들'은 사업을 다각화하여 요즘은 석유 회사라기보다 에너지 회사가 되었고, OPEC 국가들은 다른 산업을 배제하려고(→개발하려고) 시급히 시도하고 있다.
필수 단어
1. consumer[명]소비자, 소비처
2. transport[명]운송, 수송
3. internal combustion engine[구]내연기관
4. efficient[형]효율적인
5. consumption[명]소비
6. polluting[형]오염시키는
7. fuel cell[구]연료전지
8. momentum[명]추진력, 탄력
9. multinational[명]다국적 기업
10. prototype[명]시제품, 원형
11. race[동]경쟁하다, 다투다
12. performance[명]성능, 성과
13. profit[명]이익, 수익
14. depend upon[구]~에 달려 있다
15. breakthrough[명]획기적 돌파구
16. dramatically[부]급격히, 극적으로
17. signal[동]알리다, 신호하다
18. demand[명]수요
19. supply[명]공급
20. stand to[구]~하게 될 가능성이 있다

STEP 01

본문과 해석
본문 + 해석 + 핵심 어휘 정리
동의어 ≈
1.consumer = user, buyer
2.transport = transportation, shipping
3.internal combustion engine = ICE
4.efficient = effective, economical
5.consumption = use, intake
반의어 ↔
1.consumer ↔ producer
2.transport ↔ —
3.internal combustion engine ↔ electric motor
4.efficient ↔ wasteful, inefficient
5.consumption ↔ production
영영풀이
1.consumer: a person or thing that uses up a product or resource
2.efficient: working well without wasting time, energy, or fuel
3.breakthrough: an important new discovery or sudden advance
4.threat: a danger or possibility of harm
5.diversify: to start to do a wider range of things or businesses
필수 표현
1.depend upon: ~에 달려 있다
2.stand to: ~하게 될 처지이다
3.look for: ~을 찾다, 모색하다
4.race to: ~을 앞다투어 하다
5.not anything like: ~와 전혀 같지 않다

STEP 6 영문 배열 13문항
1
The major consumer of oil is transport.
2
But consider what has happened over the last 30 years or so to the technology involved in producing the internal combustion engine.
3
Because oil is expensive, car engines today are far more efficient in their consumption of fuel (and far less polluting) than they were in 1972.
4
The cars that Asia buys tomorrow will certainly not be anything like those Americans use today.
5
Americans will not buy today's cars tomorrow either.
6
In fact, if the price of oil does rise much further then fuel cell technology (which produces energy from water!) will receive yet another momentum.
7
The big car multinationals have already produced the prototype motors — they are currently racing to try and get prices down and engine performances up.
8
Their future profits depend upon it.
9
Imagine now if there is a breakthrough in fuel cell technology.
10
What would happen to oil prices?
11
They would fall dramatically — signalling much less demand than supply — and oil companies and OPEC oil producers would stand to lose much income.
12
The fact that this threat is real is driving the producers to look for alternative sources of income.
13
The 'oil majors' have diversified and are now more energy companies than oil companies these days and the OPEC countries are urgently attempting to exclude other industries.
